TEST FIXTURE: GERMANY CUSTOMS REGULATION
DOCUMENT CLASSIFICATION: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE (NOT REAL REGULATION)
DOCUMENT ID: doc_germany_customs_001
COUNTRY: Germany
DOCUMENT TYPE: Customs Regulation
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2026-01-01
VERSION: v2.4

SECTION 1: OVERVIEW AND SCOPE
This document outlines standard customs clearance requirements for commercial import shipments entering the Federal Republic of Germany through major air and ocean ports of entry.

SECTION 2: MANDATORY IMPORT DOCUMENTATION
All standard commercial shipments entering Germany must include the following primary documentation:
1. Commercial Invoice: Must detail the full buyer and seller addresses, EORI number, description of goods in German or English, HS tariff codes (minimum 6 digits), unit values, currency, and Incoterms 2020.
2. Packing List: Must accompany all multi-package shipments and state gross weight, net weight, package dimensions, and exact carton counts.
3. Customs Declaration (Atlas System / Form 0747): Electronic declaration submitted prior to cargo arrival.
4. Certificate of Origin: Required for preferential duty rate claims under applicable bilateral trade agreements.

SECTION 3: TARIFF AND TAX ASSESSMENT
Import duty rates are calculated based on the CIF (Cost, Insurance, and Freight) value. Value-Added Tax (Einfuhrumsatzsteuer) of 19% standard rate or 7% reduced rate applies to qualifying goods upon entry.

SECTION 4: COMPLIANCE CONTACT AND AUDIT
Customs audits require documentation retention for a minimum of 10 years following customs clearance.
